title: Abelianity of quasi-coherent modules on a flat algebraic-space groupoid
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ a groupoid in algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-space-groupoid, def-trf-algebraic-space], with $c:R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$. Suppose $s,t$ are flat: after etale scheme charts of source and target their scheme representatives are flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. On the small etale ringed sites use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], quasi-coherent modules [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and tensor pullbacks [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Define $\mathcal C$ to have objects $(M,\alpha)$ with $M\in\operatorname{QCoh}(U)$ and $\alpha:t^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}s^*M$, with $e^*\alpha=1$ and $c^*\alpha=\operatorname{pr}_1^*\alpha\circ\operatorname{pr}_0^*\alpha$ on $R\times_{s,U,t}R$ under the canonical pullback identifications. A morphism $v:(M,\alpha)\to(N,\beta)$ is a module map with $s^*v\circ\alpha=\beta\circ t^*v$; identities, composition and addition are those of the underlying module maps. Then $\mathcal C$ is an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. The forgetful functor to $\operatorname{QCoh}(U)$ computes kernels and cokernels as the underlying module-sheaf kernels and cokernels with their induced descent data. No quasi-compactness, finiteness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-flat-space-groupoid-kernels-cokernels] to the given $S,U,R,s,t,e,i,c$. Its groupoid convention is the same: $c$ composes the second arrow followed by the first, and the descent isomorphism goes from $t^*M$ to $s^*M$. Its objects obey exactly $e^*\alpha=1$ and $c^*\alpha=\operatorname{pr}_1^*\alpha\circ\operatorname{pr}_0^*\alpha$; its morphisms obey exactly $s^*v\circ\alpha=\beta\circ t^*v$. Thus its category and forgetful functor are the category and functor of this statement, with the same underlying identities, composition and addition. Its hypotheses require just the stated groupoid and flatness of $s,t$ on etale scheme charts. The cited statement gives abelianity and computes both kernels and cokernels as small-etale module-sheaf kernels and cokernels endowed with their induced groupoid isomorphisms, including quasi-coherence of those underlying modules. These are all the required conclusions. Its explicit absence of quasi-compactness, finite-presentation, separation and Noetherian assumptions confirms that no extra hypothesis is used.
